newsitem.title: UK: ABF retreats from recent record peak.
newsitem.headline: ABF retreats from recent record peak.

text.p: Shares in Associated British Foods Plc were the biggest percentage fallers in the FTSE 100 index by midsession on Thursday, as buying dried up after recent sharp gains, dealers said.
The stock, which hit a record 578p on June 17, was marked down 25p or 4.4 percent at 539 by 1140 GMT in thin volume of 223,902 shares.
"They have been quite a firm feature but now the market just doesn't want to buy," said one head of equity trading.
Dealers said they were not aware of any specific negative story on the stock today.

ABF shares were driven higher in recent months amid hopes that the company will use its growing cash pile for an acquisition. In February it sold its Irish supermarkets unit to Tesco Plc for 630 million stg.
The company has also in the past been seen as a potential bid target as the food sector consolidates.
At their recent high, ABF shares were up some 28 percent since their year's low of 453p set on January 9.
